title: Navigate Offroad, Exact Rider Dots and Better Maps
intro: Navigate is a new offroad map for riding on your own: record and share your own trails, rate trails other riders mapped, and measure distances. Rider dots sit on each rider's exact position at every zoom, are easier to see and point the way each rider is heading. Ride Mode's route line shows every rider in running order, Full Map gives you the map with nothing in the way, and a new button brings the map back to you. Roads and trails show from farther out, ride times take a few taps, rides can be planned for 2027 and beyond, sharing can stay on until you turn it off, and any sheet swipes down to close. New badges and ranks reward the rides you lead, join and finish, Out Riding shows which riders are out near you so you can message them, and you can add riders as friends.
whatsNew:
What's new in 1.0.3:

• Nav Mode: offroad map and your own trails.
• Badges and ranks for leading, riding and miles.
• Out Riding + Friends: see who's out and message them.
• Rider dots stay put and show heading.
• Full Map; riders in order on the route line.
• Ride Mode opens on you; Center on Me.
• Trails show from farther out.
• Faster time picker; plan rides in 2027+.
• Share location until you turn it off.
• Swipe down to close any sheet.
• Emergency: hold Alert My Group.
• Update alerts.

notes.text: Navigate, an offroad map for when you're not on a group ride. See every trail and road with your speed and elevation, draw trails with the distance finder or record them, add photos, and keep them on your phone or share them with every rider with a name, difficulty and the vehicles that fit. Trails other riders shared show as mint dotted lines on every map (turn them off in Settings). Tap one to rate its quality and how accurate the line is; trails rated inaccurate are hidden and the mapper is told. With Pro, record and share your trails and turn any trail into a group ride's route; the map, measuring and ratings are free.

Badges and ranks. Earn Bronze, Silver and Gold badges for leading rides (Trail Boss), riding at the rear (Tail Gunner), riding with a group (Crew Rider), your miles (Mile Eater) and the trails you share and rate (Trailblazer, Mapmaker, Trail Scout). Your levels add up to a rank from Rookie to Legend. See them on the You tab, get a notification when you earn one, and spot each rider's top badge beside their name.

Out Riding. Heading out, or at a park for the weekend? Switch on Out Riding from the Groups tab to see which riders are out near you right now and roughly how far away they are (never where), then send them a message. By default only riders you've ridden with can see you; pick Everyone Nearby to meet anyone at the same park who chose the same. It's off until you switch it on and turns itself off.

Friends. Add the riders you ride with as friends from Friends on the Groups tab, from a ride's Going list, from Out Riding or from a conversation, or share your friend link with anyone. Friends see each other in Out Riding and can message any time. There's no search by name, and being friends never shares where you are.
Full Map in Ride Mode. Tap Full Map to hide the ride name, banners, buttons and riders list. A slim bar keeps the route line, EMERGENCY and Menus, which brings everything back.
A small arrow on each moving rider's dot shows which way they're heading, and it stays true when you turn the map. Stopped riders show a plain dot.

If an update ever has a problem, the app can tell you: an About This Version card on the home screen explains what's wrong, Update Available lets you know a fix is out, and Please Update OnMyLead asks you to update (with Not Now, so you're never locked out on the trail).
Ride Mode has a Center on Me button. Tap it to bring the map back to your location. It keeps your zoom, and zooms in to riding distance if you were zoomed far out.
Share your location until you turn it off. Until I Turn It Off no longer stops after 24 hours, and ride shares get the same choice (they still end when the ride ends).
Pick an End Date when you share your location: choose a day and time up to a year out.

The route line in Ride Mode shows every sharing rider's dot in running order, rear to front, and riders bunched together line up side by side instead of hiding each other. The leader is blue, the tail gunner purple, and you red. Tap a dot for the rider's name and place.
Rider dots are easier to see on satellite, topo and the dark map: each rider is a bold white ring with a dark name tag, and the leader is a bigger solid blue dot with a blue name tag.
Pick times by tapping instead of typing: tap AM or PM, the hour and the minute. Works for Meet At, Departure Time, Expected Finish, a planned stop's time and Stop Sharing At.

Swipe down to close any sheet: a new waypoint, Riders, Directions, Share Your Location, Emergency, a report, the Pro prompt and the ride's QR code. In a long sheet the first swipe scrolls back to the top, and if the keyboard is up it puts the keyboard away first.
Roads and dirt trails show on the Ride Mode map from about 15 miles across, so you no longer have to zoom way in to see them. When you're zoomed far out, the longest trails are drawn first.
Create a Ride takes dates in 2027 and later, up to three years out. On the calendar you can type a date or jump straight to any month and year.
The You tab shows your active location share and when it ends.

Rider dots in Ride Mode now sit on each rider's exact position and stay there as you zoom in and out. Before, every dot was drawn a little to the right of the rider, so riders who were together looked spread out. Waypoints, planned stops and search pins are placed exactly too.

Emergency in Ride Mode: Alert My Group now fills a bar while you hold it and says Keep Holding, so it no longer looks like nothing happens. A quick tap tells you the alert was not sent, and the screen closes as soon as the alert goes out so you can see who has it.
Trail and road lines no longer flash or disappear while you move or zoom the map.
Tablets show trails at the same zoom as phones. They used to appear only when zoomed in much closer.
Opening Help and Support, Contact Us, Terms or Privacy no longer shows an "Expo Head" alert.

Ride Mode's map opens centered on you, zoomed in close enough to see nearby trails, instead of over a random spot. If your phone is still finding you, the map centers as soon as it does, unless you've already moved it.

title: Android, Battery Saver and Trail Names
intro: OnMyLead arrives on Android phones and tablets. This update also adds Battery Saver, a ride calendar, Report a Bug, and trails that are easier to read.
whatsNew:
What's new in 1.0.1:

• Battery Saver: choose how often your phone sends its location while you share.
• Create a Ride has a calendar: pick any day up to a year out.
• Trails are bolder, show their names, and closed trails are marked in red.
• Search for a place on the waypoints map.
• Report a Bug from the You tab, with a screenshot.
• Ride Mode tells you when location is turned off for OnMyLead.

notes.text: OnMyLead is on Google Play for Android phones and tablets, with the same rides, live map, chat and Pro plan as on iPhone and iPad.
Battery Saver on the You tab lets you choose how often your phone sends its location while you share: Best Accuracy, Balanced or Max Battery Saver.
Create a Ride has a Calendar button to pick any day from today up to a year out, plus Sat and Sun quick picks for the coming weekend.
Report a Bug on the You tab sends us your message with a screenshot, your phone model and app version, so problems get fixed faster.
Trails are bolder and easier to see, with trail and road names on the map. Closed roads and trails, including today's seasonal closures, show in red with a Closed note.
Search for a park, trailhead, town or address on the waypoints map, the same way as in the route builder.
If you turn off location for OnMyLead while sharing, Ride Mode now tells you with a Location Is Off notice instead of saying you're still sharing.

title: First Release
intro: The first OnMyLead: plan a ride, bring your crew, and keep everyone together on one live map.
whatsNew:
Welcome to OnMyLead, the group ride app.

• Create a ride with a meeting point, time and route.
• Invite riders with a link, code or QR code.
• See your group on one live map in Ride Mode.
• Share your location only for the ride, and stop anytime.
• Ride chat, status buttons, polls and Ride Bubble alerts.
• Draw routes; with Pro, import GPX and save offline maps.
• Find rides near you and follow leaders.
• Works on iPhone and iPad.

notes.text: Create a ride with a meeting point, time, route and who can join, then share it with a link, code or QR code.
Ride Mode puts the whole group on one live map, with status buttons, ride chat, polls and Ride Bubble alerts when someone falls behind.
Location sharing is per ride and temporary. Your exact location is never public, and you can stop sharing anytime.
Draw a route and add waypoints and planned stops. With Pro, import GPX files and save maps for offline use.
Find a ride near you and follow leaders you ride with. With Pro, keep your regular crew together in a riding group with its own chat.
Free lets you create one ride a month and join as many as you like, with every safety feature included. Pro adds unlimited rides, offline maps, GPX import and riding groups, with a 30-day free trial.
iPad gets its own layouts: the live map with a riders sidebar, and split views for rides and routes.
